title: **Rapid extraction of living primary veins from the leaves of _Arabidopsis thaliana_**
protocol: Select an expanded leaf for the procedure.
Place the apical part of the selected leaf on a block of agar (1% w/v).
Make an arc-like incision through the upper and lateral epidermis of the petiole, positioned 4-8 mm from the center of the rosette.
Do not make an incision on the basal petiole surface.
Create a second similar incision up to 4 mm from the first incision towards the leaf tip.
Make a perpendicular cut through the upper epidermis to join the two previous incisions.
Gently remove extravascular tissues in the region of the incisions using small forceps and a scalpel.
Ensure that the manipulations do not damage the vasculature.
This procedure typically takes 2-5 minutes to complete.
Select an expanded leaf.
Cut off the leaf blade just above the petiole/blade junction, leaving a few millimeters of the leaf blade.
Discard the apical part of the leaf blade.
Make gentle incisions through the upper (adaxial) and lateral epidermis near the base of the petiole using a scalpel.
Avoid making any incision on the underside of the petiole.
Gently pull away the cut end near the petiole/lamina junction using thumb and forefinger to expose the midvein.
Quickly excise the exposed vein for immediate use or rapid freezing in liquid nitrogen.
Make a ring-like incision through the upper and lateral epidermis of the petiole of the leaf 4 - 8 mm from the center of the rosette.
Gently pull the leaf away from the center of the plant using thumb and forefinger.
Place a block of 1% (w/v) agar in 0.5 x Murashige Skoog medium on the soil below the exposed vein to prevent desiccation.
Place a strip of filter paper previously soaked in 0.5 x MS medium on the agar block below the vein to enhance visibility and prevent desiccation.
Allow plants to recover for 1 hour in humidified Plexiglas boxes before conducting experiments.
